sections.title: Definition & Epidemiology
sections.content: Fungal keratitis (FK) is a sight-threatening infection of the corneal stroma. Prevalence is highest in tropical climates and agricultural settings. Filamentous fungi (e.g., Fusarium, Aspergillus) account for ~70% of cases, while yeasts (e.g., Candida) are more common in temperate climates or compromised ocular surfaces.

sections.title: Red Flags: When to Suspect Fungal Etiology
content: History of vegetative trauma or topical steroid use

sections.title: Investigation Workup Protocol
content: Step 1: Corneal scraping from ulcer base and edge
Step 2: Immediate Gram stain (for bacteria) and KOH/Calcofluor White prep
Step 3: Inoculation onto Sabouraud Dextrose Agar (SDA) and Blood Agar
Step 4: Confocal Microscopy (In-vivo) if culture negative but suspicious
Step 5: PCR for fungal DNA if available (high sensitivity)

sections.title: Treatment Algorithm
content: Filamentous Fungi: Topical Natamycin 5% (First-line) or Voriconazole 1%
Yeast (Candida): Topical Amphotericin B 0.15% or Voriconazole 1%
Adjunctive Therapy: Oral Fluconazole 200mg BID or Voriconazole 200mg BID
Management Note: Avoid topical corticosteroids initially; taper only when fungal load is significantly reduced and re-epithelialization is observed.

content.explanation: F - Filamentous, E - Edge (Feathery), A - Agricultural trauma, T - Topical steroids, H - Hypopyon, E - Epithelial defect, R - Resistant to drops, S - Satellite lesions.

sections.title: Landmark Clinical Study: Mycotic Ulcer Treatment Trial (MUTT)
content: MUTT-I: Natamycin 5% demonstrated superior efficacy over Voriconazole 1% for filamentous keratitis (Fusarium).
MUTT-II: Oral Voriconazole did not improve outcomes compared to placebo in cases already receiving topical Natamycin.
